title: Stage-isolated delivery entities and bounded artifact handoffs
summary: Add immutable RunStore-backed stage aggregate roots, content-addressed bounded handoff manifests, a replaceable active-stage projection, and a non-destructive singleton migration adapter while preserving all R-0003 authority, evidence, and fail-closed worktree-cleanup invariants.

current_state.summary: The product persists one mutable loop.json, track switching moves that singleton record, RunStore v3 already supplies revision-checked atomic manifests and R-0003 receipts, review_evidence already supplies confined content-addressed artifacts, and current status/Retro paths can read singleton or full-trace state. There is no independently addressable stage aggregate, immutable lineage, split transaction, bounded inter-stage manifest, or conservative singleton migration.

alternatives.name: Extend singleton move and restore
alternatives.description: Add lifecycle and handoff fields to loop.json and teach track.py to move a larger set of per-stage files.

gains: Smallest superficial code and CLI change
Reuses the existing common loop lock
costs: A moved mutable record is not an independently addressable immutable aggregate
Split children still share one mutable history and one context-bearing loop record
Restore can reclassify predecessor state and cannot prove bounded successor startup
tradeoffs.revisit_when: R-0004 is narrowed to strictly sequential single-child execution with no immutable lineage, split, or bounded-context requirements.

alternatives.name: RunStore immutable stage aggregates with projection adapter
alternatives.description: Persist content-addressed stage and handoff objects, atomically index their heads/lineage/operation receipts in RunStore v4, derive a replaceable active projection, and temporarily adapt legacy loop/track readers.

gains: Reuses existing revision checks, locks, atomic replacement, canonical run roots, and artifact verification
Makes terminal history, successors, and split children immutable and independently addressable
Makes successor startup and status depend only on bounded manifests and summaries
costs: Requires a deliberate v3-to-v4 migration and temporary dual-reader
Adds three focused domain modules and explicit projection-repair semantics
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Multiple distributed writers or arbitrary temporal replay queries require an event log as the primary source of truth.

alternatives.name: Full event-sourced stage graph
alternatives.description: Make lifecycle, split, handoff, and projection changes append-only events and rebuild stage aggregates through replay and snapshots.

gains: Rich temporal queries and a complete append-only transition stream
Natural extension point for future multi-writer coordination
costs: Requires ordering, replay, upcaster, snapshot, compaction, and migration governance
Creates new paths for startup, status, or Retro to accidentally scale with predecessor history
Disproportionate to current local revision-checked writers
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Multi-region writers, temporal queries, or event-level external integrations are accepted product requirements and snapshot governance is funded.

decision: Select RunStore-backed immutable stage aggregates because they are the smallest existing transaction model that can make stage identity, terminal outcomes, lineage, splits, bounded handoffs, retry idempotency, and conservative migration mechanically true. Immutable objects are written before one authoritative manifest revision updates their index, lineage, active projection, and operation receipt. The active pointer and legacy loop/track shapes are projections only. Full event sourcing is deferred because it adds replay and snapshot complexity without improving R-0004's bounded default reads.

contracts.description: taskplane.stage/v1 gives each stage a stable identity, isolated execution root, immutable indexed head, active-to-exactly-one-terminal transition, and idempotent lifecycle receipt.
taskplane.stage-handoff/v1 is the sole default inter-stage context boundary and carries bounded authority-bound metadata plus explicitly selected verified content-addressed artifacts.
The immutable indexed predecessor, parent, child, handoff, and outcome relations are authoritative; the active-stage projection is rebuildable and non-authoritative.

Every stage start, resume, terminalization, handoff, split, migration resolution, and explicit artifact reuse binds the exact run, repository/worktree, requirement/design revision, actor/session, and authority revision and re-resolves authority before commit.

Recovery may replay an identical authorized operation receipt or rebuild the active projection; it cannot select outcomes, add artifacts, reopen terminal stages, manufacture children, approve gates, or broaden R-0003 cleanup.
Handoffs reuse the existing immutable review artifact identity, digest, byte-count, confinement, and canonical-run storage checks so evidence remains verifiable after a worker tree is removed.

acceptance_map.criterion: Every stage entity has a stable stage id, requirement revision, stage kind, parent or predecessor links, bounded input manifest, independent execution tree, and exactly one terminal outcome of done, closed, or discarded.
acceptance_map.design_element: taskplane.stage/v1 aggregate schema, immutable indexed heads, unique canonical execution roots, 64 KiB input bound, and active-to-one-terminal state machine in stage_entities.py.
acceptance_map.validation: Schema/property tests generate every kind/link/outcome combination; reject missing/duplicate identities, reused roots, missing revisions, oversized inputs, zero/multiple outcomes, and any terminal-to-active transition.

acceptance_map.criterion: Done requires the declared deliverables and completion evidence; closed requires an attributable reason explaining why no further work is required; discarded requires an attributable reason explaining why its results must not be consumed. No terminal entity can silently return to active.
acceptance_map.design_element: Outcome-specific terminal guards, immutable terminal head, attributable actor/time/reason, discarded default_consumable=false, and no reopen command.
acceptance_map.validation: Outcome matrix verifies done rejects missing deliverables/evidence, closed/discarded reject absent attribution or reasons, discarded input is excluded by default, and all later transition attempts reject without head mutation.

acceptance_map.criterion: Starting a next stage creates a new execution tree and consumes only a versioned manifest plus explicitly selected content-addressed artifacts from predecessor stages; prior agents, conversations, event logs, tool transcripts, leases, and runtime state are not inherited as context.
acceptance_map.design_element: Fresh per-stage execution root and dispatcher payload serializer that accepts only taskplane.stage-handoff/v1 plus verified selected refs and an explicit exclusion list.
acceptance_map.validation: Cross-host startup goldens and hostile fixture seed predecessor agents/transcripts/logs/leases/runtime/secrets; successor bytes contain none, root id differs, and only declared verified fingerprints resolve.

acceptance_map.criterion: A handoff manifest records producer stage id and outcome, requirement and design revisions, target and commit identity where applicable, contracts, deliverables, evidence references, artifact fingerprints, exclusions, and the actor and time authorizing continuation.
acceptance_map.design_element: taskplane.stage-handoff/v1 canonical schema, 64 KiB/64-ref bounds, content fingerprint, authority binding, target applicability rule, and artifact verifier.
acceptance_map.validation: Canonical schema matrix requires every named field, conditional target/commit identity, exact contract relations, digest/bytes, exclusions and attribution; tamper, omission, path escape, oversize and stale-authority cases fail closed.

acceptance_map.criterion: Product, Design, Review, Evaluation, and other non-build work can terminate closed or discarded without creating an implementation stage, while their retained artifacts remain addressable for audit or later explicit reuse.
acceptance_map.design_element: Stage-kind-independent terminal command, optional successor, immutable artifact retention, and separately authorized explicit fingerprint reuse that does not mutate the predecessor outcome.
acceptance_map.validation: Per-kind tests close/discard without a build child, verify zero active successor and retained artifact reads, reject default discarded consumption, and permit exact later reuse only with new actor/time/authority/reason.

acceptance_map.criterion: Splitting a deliverable closes the parent with a split reason and creates two or more independently addressable child stage entities with explicit artifact subsets, dependencies, budgets, and lifecycles; one child outcome cannot mutate sibling or parent history.
acceptance_map.design_element: Single split_stage RunStore transaction, deterministic child ids, >=2 child guard, explicit subsets/dependencies/budgets, separate heads/roots, and parent closed reason_code=split.
acceptance_map.validation: Property/concurrency/crash tests cover 2..N children, duplicate retry, subset violations and races; compare parent/sibling fingerprints before and after one child terminalizes and assert only that child's head changes.

acceptance_map.criterion: The active-stage pointer is a replaceable projection only. Starting, resuming, splitting, or terminalizing a stage never overwrites or reclassifies a predecessor entity, and history lists every terminal and active entity with lineage.
acceptance_map.design_element: Authoritative stage_heads/lineage index, rebuildable active_stage_projection with sorted ids/optional foreground, immutable predecessor heads, and cursor-paged history summaries.
acceptance_map.validation: Delete/corrupt projection and rebuild from heads; mutation sequence compares every predecessor fingerprint, detects ambiguity rather than choosing, and lists all active/terminal entities with exact parent/predecessor/child/handoff links.

acceptance_map.criterion: Crash, duplicate event, reconnect, and retry fixtures prove stage terminalization, handoff creation, and split creation are atomic and idempotent, with no duplicate child, lost artifact, reopened terminal stage, or ambiguous active pointer.
acceptance_map.design_element: Expected run revision, request-fingerprinted operation id, write-object-before-index protocol, one atomic heads/lineage/projection/receipt commit, and receipt-authoritative replay.
acceptance_map.validation: Failure injection at every write/replace/journal boundary plus duplicate/reconnect/race fixtures assert one receipt, one semantic transition, exact artifact conservation, deterministic children, terminal immutability, and projection=heads equality.

acceptance_map.criterion: Dashboard, status, review, sign-off, and Retro show the current stage, predecessor outcome, artifact handoff, and child lineage from bounded summaries without loading predecessor execution trees.
acceptance_map.design_element: <=16 KiB terminal summary, <=100-row cursor page, lineage_summary API, text-first renderers, and Retro aggregation over terminal metrics rather than trace scans.
acceptance_map.validation: Instrument file opens and assert each surface renders all named fields and pending actions from summaries while predecessor execution roots raise if opened; test page bounds, text-only parity, and corrupt-summary failures.

acceptance_map.criterion: As irrelevant predecessor history grows from ten to one hundred thousand events, the default successor startup payload remains byte-identical and bounded to the manifest plus explicitly selected artifacts; startup work and token use do not scale with predecessor runtime history.
acceptance_map.design_element: Pure canonical startup serializer over the handoff object and selected refs only, with manifest/ref/byte/token telemetry and zero predecessor-tree dependency.
acceptance_map.validation: 10-vs-100000-event benchmark asserts identical SHA-256 and bytes, same read count, zero predecessor-root opens, <=64 KiB manifest, <=64 refs, and stable startup work/token estimate within fixed measurement tolerance.

acceptance_map.criterion: A migration converts singleton loop records into stage entities without losing requirements, tasks, decisions, evidence, commits, reviews, or audit history; ambiguous legacy state is preserved with an explicit unknown reason rather than guessed as pending, done, closed, or discarded.
acceptance_map.design_element: Idempotent stage_migration source fingerprint, immutable legacy source artifacts, conservation manifest, deterministic known projections, taskplane.legacy-unknown/v1 sentinel, and verified receipt before adapter cutover.
acceptance_map.validation: Golden and generative legacy fixtures compare before/after identity/count/fingerprint sets for every named record class, replay identically after crashes, and require explicit unknown_reason for ambiguity with no guessed lifecycle or lost source bytes.

risks.risk: A projection is accidentally treated as lifecycle authority and revives or hides a stage.
risks.mitigation: All writes require immutable indexed heads; projection equality is verified/rebuilt under lock, ambiguity stops dispatch, and tests delete/corrupt it.

risks.risk: The legacy adapter becomes a second writer and reintroduces singleton overwrite semantics.
risks.mitigation: After migration receipt, adapter APIs are read-only projections and every loop/track mutation routes through stage_entities; AST/runtime tests prohibit move/restore writes on v4 runs.

risks.risk: A handoff leaks predecessor transcript, secret, path, approval, or runtime authority.
risks.mitigation: Closed schema, redacted canonical refs, explicit exclusions, authority rebinding, byte/ref bounds, hostile-input tests, and startup serializers with no predecessor-tree handle.

risks.risk: Split or retry creates duplicate children or partially terminalizes the parent.
risks.mitigation: Deterministic child ids and one request-fingerprinted expected-revision RunStore commit cover parent head, children, lineage, projection, and receipt.

risks.risk: Legacy ambiguity is silently classified to make migration appear complete.
risks.mitigation: Unknown sentinel is the only allowed ambiguous projection, carries an explicit reason and retained source fingerprint, and cannot be default successor input.

risks.risk: Stage terminalization broadens or prematurely triggers destructive R-0003 worktree cleanup.
risks.mitigation: Lifecycle contains no cleanup call; cleanup remains a separate exact-registration/merged-tip/re-resolved-main proof with all retention negatives, no force, and durable outcomes.

risks.risk: Bounded summaries omit information needed by Review or Retro, causing a fallback to full predecessor traces.
risks.mitigation: Define all required review/retro metrics in the terminal summary, make predecessor-root opens fail in tests, and require an explicit audit command for details.

failure_modes.mode: Crash before the authoritative run-index commit
failure_modes.detection: No matching stage_operations receipt and indexed heads retain the previous revision; optional immutable objects are unreferenced.
failure_modes.recovery: Retry the same operation id; recompute and commit once. Do not delete orphan objects in R-0004.

failure_modes.mode: Crash after run-index commit but before diagnostic journal append
failure_modes.detection: Matching request-fingerprinted receipt and new indexed heads exist while the non-authoritative journal entry is absent.
failure_modes.recovery: Return the durable receipt and optionally append a deduplicated diagnostic entry; never repeat the semantic transition.

failure_modes.mode: Operation id is reused with different request bytes
failure_modes.detection: Stored request fingerprint differs from the retry fingerprint.
failure_modes.recovery: Fail closed with an operation-id collision; require a new id after the caller reconciles current heads.

failure_modes.mode: Active projection is missing, corrupt, stale, or ambiguous
failure_modes.detection: Projection fails schema/fingerprint validation or differs from the active states in stage_heads.
failure_modes.recovery: Stop dispatch and rebuild deterministically under the run lock; if foreground is not uniquely derivable, leave it unset and require attribution.

failure_modes.mode: Handoff artifact is missing, altered, outside the canonical store, or exceeds a declared bound
failure_modes.detection: Artifact identity/digest/byte/confinement validation or manifest size/ref count validation fails before successor creation.
failure_modes.recovery: Keep predecessor and projection unchanged; regenerate or explicitly reselect valid artifacts under a new authorization.

failure_modes.mode: Concurrent terminalize, successor, or split commands race
failure_modes.detection: Expected RunStore revision or expected stage-head fingerprint conflicts.
failure_modes.recovery: Reload heads and return an identical receipt only for the same request; otherwise reject without speculative merge.

failure_modes.mode: Legacy lifecycle or reference identity cannot be proven
failure_modes.detection: Migration classifier cannot map all source facts to one valid stage state without inference.
failure_modes.recovery: Retain source bytes and create an explicit legacy-unknown sentinel; require attributable forward resolution.

failure_modes.mode: Default status/startup path attempts to load a predecessor execution tree
failure_modes.detection: Instrumented access guard and zero-tree-open telemetry fire; 10-vs-100000-event performance fixture diverges.
failure_modes.recovery: Block release/canary, restore bounded summary/ref reader, and re-run byte-identity and cross-host tests.

failure_modes.mode: A stage transition reaches post-merge worktree cleanup without full R-0003 eligibility
failure_modes.detection: Exact revalidation finds dirty, untracked, staged, unmerged, foreign, unregistered, selected-variant, failed, active, locked, symlinked/reparse-point, path-mismatched, missing-ref, ambiguous-main, primary/main, merge-in-progress, evidence-needed, last-moment-uncertain, branch/tip-mismatched, or recorded-tip-not-ancestor state.
failure_modes.recovery: Retain the exact tree and registration plus branch, commits, requirement, design, plan, submissions, tests, review evidence, audit, and sign-off inputs; record the predicate; never force, broaden, delete a branch, or retry with stronger authority.

signals: stage id, kind, lifecycle, terminal outcome, and aggregate fingerprint
run revision, operation id, request fingerprint, and receipt status
authority revision, actor/session identity, and revalidation result
predecessor, parent, child, handoff, and active-projection fingerprints
manifest bytes, selected-reference count/bytes, startup bytes/tokens, and explicit expansion reason
projection repair count/reason and lifecycle revision conflicts
migration source/result fingerprints, conservation counts, unknown reason, and adapter mode
bounded status/Retro page sizes and predecessor execution-tree open count
R-0003 cleanup eligibility, retention predicate, merge receipt, re-resolved main tip, and removal verification
alerts: Alert and block dispatch on a terminal-reopen attempt or ambiguous active projection.
Alert on operation-id/request-fingerprint mismatch or repeated lifecycle revision conflicts.
Alert and reject on stage/handoff/artifact digest, confinement, schema, or numeric-bound failure.
Alert and block release if a default startup/status/review/sign-off/Retro path opens a predecessor execution tree or the 10-vs-100000 startup invariant diverges.
Alert and stop migration on conservation mismatch, missing retained source bytes, or ambiguous state without explicit unknown_reason.
Alert and retain on any cleanup attempt without the complete R-0003 exact registered-worktree and merged-tip proof.

rollout.strategy: Ship additive taskplane.run/v4 readers, validators, immutable objects, operation receipts, and projection repair behind a disabled flag. Run non-mutating shadow migrations and compare bounded legacy/v4 summaries and conservation sets. Enable stage-native execution for new runs, then verified migrations, then bounded dashboard/status/review/sign-off/Retro readers. Stop singleton move/restore writes only after migration/zero-tree-open telemetry and cross-host fixtures pass. Keep the legacy read adapter and retained source artifacts until a later requirement retires them.
rollout.rollback: Disable new v4 stage creation and leave immutable stage/handoff/source objects and receipts intact. Unmigrated runs may return to legacy reads; migrated runs remain v4-readable and pause mutation until re-enabled. Never reverse-collapse stage history into loop.json, reopen terminal outcomes, guess legacy unknowns, delete artifacts/branches/evidence, weaken authority/evidence binding, or broaden/force R-0003 cleanup.
